title: Contrail roadmap playbook (scratch)
content:
Meeting: Cross-team roadmap alignment — Contrail initiative (scratch)
Date: 2026-06-24 meeting (prep notes)
Attendees (TBC): Product: Lina Shah, Ethan Park; Eng: Mateo Li, Priya Singh; Applied ML: Maya Rivera, Jonah Kim; SRE: Sam Ortiz (optional)
Duration: 45m
Primary goal: Create a practical rollout/playbook for Contrail (low-latency hybrid routing + cache-first inference) that balances latency SLOs, unit cost, and model quality regressions.
Secondary goals: Agree on metrics and quick experiments we can ship in the next 6 weeks; identify owners and immediate blockers.

Background (one-liner to open meeting):
- Contrail is our planned routing layer that routes requests to cached prefixes, lite quantized variants, or full-precision models based on policy. Product wants predictable p95 latency under 180ms for chat workloads while cutting token cost by ~30% for high-frequency routes.
- Current gaps: rollout playbook is vague on canary progression, regression detection for hallucination, and which routes get cache warming.

Agenda (timeboxed):
1) 5m — Quick context + success criteria (Lina)
2) 10m — Proposed policy tiers and model variants (Maya)
3) 10m — Canary plan + traffic split mechanics (Mateo)
4) 10m — Eval & rollback signals (Priya / Jonah)
5) 5m — Action items and owners

Proposed policy tiers (draft):
- Tier A (latency-critical): prefer cache + quantized small model; fallback to full precision only on cache miss + fail-safe
- Tier B (balanced): try quantized first then cached prefix; allow slightly higher 99th percentile
- Tier C (quality-critical): always full precision; use optimistic caching only for prompts labeled stable
Notes: need mapping from route tags in Console to tiers. Product to propose default mapping for top 20 routes.

Canary plan (rough):
- Phase 0: internal-only simulation (no real traffic) — run for 48h using replay of last 72h of traffic. Owner: Mateo. Due: 2026-06-30.
- Phase 1: 0.5% real traffic, region us-west, for 24h — monitor latency/cost/quality signals. Owner: Sam. Due: 2026-07-07.
- Phase 2: 5% traffic across 2 regions, 72h — expand if stable. Owner: Mateo. Due: 2026-07-14.
- Phase 3: 25% rolling expansion with automated fallback on error spike. Owner: Lina + Eng on-call. Due: 2026-07-21.
Rollback triggers: >=2x baseline error rate OR >15% drop in objective quality metric OR p99 degradation >1.5x baseline.

Eval & regression detection (quick draft):
- Quality metrics to track: BLEU-like / task-specific scores, hallucination rate (via named-entity hallucination heuristics), user-reported feedback, and synthetic prompt set regressions.
- Short-term eval harness: Maya to assemble 250 prompt set (priority routes) and baseline scores by 2026-06-29.
- Automated checks: run nightly eval, fail build if regression > 2 std dev on critical prompts.
- Human-in-the-loop: weekly spot-check by Applied ML on sample of 200 responses when moving from Phase 1 -> Phase 2.

Operational hooks (must-have):
- Circuit breaker in routing layer that forces fallback to full-precision model for specific route ids.
- Console UI: per-route rollout toggle and per-model metric breakdown (cost/token, avg latency) — Product to file Console ticket.
- Tracing: distributed trace must include routing decision tag (cache/quant/primary) for every request.

Open questions / Risks (notes to self):
- How do we attach user-level privacy constraints to cached prefixes? (privacy team?)
- Unclear whether our quantized model variants retain safety filters — need applied ML to confirm.
- Cost accounting: will token-level cost attribution show savings at route granularity today? If not, finance needs a quick mapping.
- Risk of cold-starts for cached prefixes in low-frequency routes — consider warm-up scheduler.

Immediate action items (single-line, owner, due):
- Assemble priority route list (top 20 by qps) and propose default tier mapping — Lina — 2026-06-26
- Run replay simulation with current traffic snapshot and baseline metrics export — Mateo — 2026-06-30
- Build 250-prompt regression harness, label critical prompts, baseline scores — Maya — 2026-06-29
- Create Console ticket for per-route rollout toggle + metric panel — Ethan Park — 2026-06-25
- Draft privacy checklist for cached prefixes and hand off to security — Priya Singh — 2026-06-28
- Add tracing tag in routing PR and link to e2e test plan — Mateo — PR #3421 owner — 2026-06-27
- Short doc: canary escalation runbook (who to page, what to flip) — Sam Ortiz — 2026-06-27

Personal prep checklist (Lina) — notes to self:
- Bring quantization quality samples to meeting (5 examples each for conv + code) — Maya promised examples; confirm.
- Bring sample trace screenshots showing current routing paths for 3 routes.
- Bring brief sketch of UI mock for per-route toggle.
- Pre-read: Confluence contrail/overview + JIRA-1287
- Call Jonah offline to clarify hallucination heuristic thresholds before meeting (10m sync).

Meeting output expectations (what to publish after call):
- Short playbook doc: 1-pager with tiers, canary phases, and key metrics (publish to Confluence) — Lina
- Action tracker with owners + dates in Jira epic JIRA-1287 — Ethan
- PR list for initial changes (routing tag, tracing, console panel, eval harness) — Mateo + Maya

Notes about tone/language for the meeting:
- Keep decisions as reversible as possible — prefer timeboxed canaries over big bangs.
- Focus conversation on measurable signals, not opinions. If we disagree, propose an experiment and agree the metric.

Misc fragments/brainstorm (scratch):
- Could we have a routing ‘cost budget’ per tenant that prevents tier A for cheap-paying customers? probably later.
- Consider cache TTLs per route type; maybe short TTL for user-generated prompts, long TTL for system prompts.
- Might want a lightweight contract: "Contrail minimum viable invariant" (p95 <180ms for Tier A, cost delta target -30% for top routes)

End of scratch. Will convert to cleaned playbook after meeting and tag owners in epic.
